page: Amazon Web Services i4i.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.5 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is configured at 32.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. The instance includes a bundled 937 GB local NVMe SSD directly attached for high I/O workloads, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. No hardware GPUs are included.

Benchmark results highlight balanced single-threaded performance paired with moderate compute capacity. In single-core metrics, the instance achieves average results across the board, scoring 1890.28 in stress-ng and 1590.0 in Geekbench single-core, alongside single-threaded gzip compression at 27.91 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded CPU output remains constrained by the 4 vCPU topology, reflected in lower-quartile stress-ng multi-core (3856.04) and Geekbench multi-core (3429.0) scores. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth registers 29.32 GB/sec for reads and 24.65 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused metrics, Redis SET throughput reaches 3.93 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 6.32 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the i4i.xlarge trades high multi-core computational horsepower for fast local NVMe storage and substantial memory density per core. Because compute capacity is tied to 2 physical cores, CPU-heavy parallel batch jobs yield modest returns relative to compute-focused instances. However, the tight integration of local low-latency NVMe storage and generous RAM makes this hardware profile well suited for storage-bound applications. The primary operational fit includes transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, caching systems, and read-intensive storage pipelines requiring fast local disk access.
description: Amazon Web Services i4i.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, configured with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a dedicated 937 GB local NVMe SSD, alongside 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Compute evaluation indicates average single-core throughput, demonstrated by a 1590.0 Geekbench single-core score, alongside constrained multi-core performance typical of a 4-vCPU layout. Memory read bandwidth reaches 29.32 GB/sec on uncached blocks, and Redis benchmarks produce 3.93 million operations per second. The hardware allocation favors data locality and read/write speeds over heavy parallel processing, making the i4i.xlarge a precise fit for transactional relational databases, NoSQL stores, caching layers, and search index operations requiring low-latency local solid-state storage.
